look_here_first: Look at the leaf axil. Drummond's ruellia has purple flowers/cymes essentially sessile in the axils rather than raised on a terminal stalk. The ovate leaves and stems have short fine pubescence, not the conspicuous long hairs of R. humilis. If fruit is present, the capsule's only 2–4 seeds are a powerful confirmation.

lookalikes.differences: Ruellia ciliatiflora: R. ciliatiflora (= R. nudiflora) raises its flowers on conspicuous terminal/upper-axillary peduncles and is much less hairy. Ruellia humilis: Both have nearly sessile axillary flowers, but R. humilis is conspicuously long-pilose with obvious individual hairs along stems and leaf margins; R. drummondiana is finely short-pubescent and has only 2–4 seeds. Ruellia simplex: Mexican petunia has long narrow lanceolate leaves and typically taller, more linear architecture; it is a common non-native landscape escape.
